label: debug-switch-or-output-left-on
name: Debug macro flipped on, debug output unguarded or routed through the wrong switch, debug-only include unguarded, trace volume raised on a production path
description: What breaks: a commented-out `// #define DEBUG_*` becomes active (DEBUG_HWATTN 2789808472 'leaving enabled intentionally?', DEBUG_GET_ALLKV + MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG 2759894229, DEBUG_HWATTN_CMD_GEN 2759903853, LOG_TOKEN_TIMES 3124878965 'can we comment this back out before merge?'); a debug_hexdump or spdlog::debug is added where siblings sit under #ifdef WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS or the file's dbg_*_log macro (2719160746, 2719161128, 2737832765); new log calls use an older sibling macro (dbg_hwattn_cmds_log) where the same diff defined dbg_wlr_log for this category (3405973171, 3405974281 'here too maybe?'); a log line carries a developer tag ('MRC allocated shard' 3002085391 'still need this log?'); a debug_string prints fields only when tok_ix > 4000 with no explanation (2915186372); a 745-line debug-only header is included unconditionally while its only use is under #ifdef DEBUG_GET_ALLKV (2737953233); a TRACE_EVENT moves from 'driver-detail' to the always-on 'driver' category while the Perfetto buffer already overflows (3456320516). Procedure: diff lines matching ^\+#define (DEBUG|LOG_|TRACE|VERBOSE|MORE_) or ^\+// -> ^\+#define; added dump/debug-log calls in h/ and src/ compared with the guard the file uses for siblings; call sites in the diff that use an older category macro when the diff defines a newer one; includes whose every use is under a debug guard; TRACE_EVENT category changes. Ask form: 'intend to leave this enabled?', 'wrap in #ifdef X?', 'still need this log?'.
disposition_reason: No existing check looks at debug switches or log guards; 13 rows over 8 PRs, mostly regex-detectable.
agent_feasibility: yes: regex over added lines plus a per-file lookup of the existing guard macro; the Perfetto buffer-pressure judgement (3456320516) needs runtime knowledge.

members.concern: A debug_hexdump call in the new K-write guard runs unconditionally while the sibling V-write guard wraps its hexdump in `#ifdef WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS`; Wade asks to wrap this one the same way so the debug dump is compiled out by default.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a call to a dump/hexdump/debug-print function (debug_hexdump, debug_bf16dump, spdlog::debug with large payload) in a production header or source path, and the same file defines a compile-time debug macro (`// #define WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS`, `#ifdef DEBUG_*`) that guards sibling calls.
detection.procedure: grep -n '#ifdef\|#define' on the touched file to list the debug macros; grep -n 'debug_hexdump\|debug_bf16dump\|dump_' on the diff's added lines; for each hit check whether the enclosing lines sit inside one of those #ifdef blocks.
detection.question: Is every added debug dump on a production path guarded by the same compile-time macro the file already uses for its siblings?

members.note: At the approved head hwattention.hpp:33 has `// #define WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS` (off by default) and the K guard's hexdump is inside `#ifdef WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS` at :407, so the author applied it. Author's reply says the fix existed locally but a crash prevented the push.

detection.trigger: An added or un-commented line defines a debug/logging macro (#define LOG_*, DEBUG_*, TRACE_*, VERBOSE), or enables a verbose log level, in a header or source file whose neighboring sibling macros are kept commented out ('uncomment to ...').
detection.procedure: Grep the diff's added lines for '#define LOG_', '#define DEBUG', 'spdlog::set_level', 'verbose = true'. For each hit, read the surrounding lines: if a comment says 'uncomment to' or the sibling macro is commented out, the enabled define is a development leftover. Check the commit list for a later 'turn off' commit.
detection.question: Does this diff turn on a logging or debug switch that the file's convention keeps off by default?

detection.trigger: A diff adds a bare numeric literal that gates whether debug or log output is produced (a threshold compare inside a debug_string, a log statement, or a dump), and the literal matches no named constant and no comment explains it.

detection.trigger: The diff adds an #include to a widely included header, and every use of the included header's symbols in that file is inside an `#ifdef <DEBUG macro>` block that is off by default.
detection.procedure: List the symbols the include provides that the file uses (grep for dump_, hwattention::, hardware::); for each use site find the enclosing #ifdef; if all uses are guarded and the macro is commented out by default (`// #define DEBUG_GET_ALLKV`), the include belongs under the guard. Count direct includers of the file (grep -rln 'self_attention.hpp' h src t) to state the blast radius.

detection.question: Does this hunk raise the number of events in the default Perfetto buffer for a path the PR's stated purpose does not require to be traced?
